chunks: And as for what was narrated - Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"The Muhrim (person in Ihram), if he kills game, upon him is its compensation (Kaffarah), and he gives the game as charity to a poor person. If he returns and kills another game, there is no compensation upon him, and Allah takes retribution from him, and the retribution is in the Hereafter."

So it does not contradict what we mentioned, because it is applied to what we preceded with regarding intentional killing, because whoever intentionally kills game after having killed (one) upon him is one compensation. And if he is forgetful, the compensation becomes obligatory upon him every time he catches the game. And that which indicates this is what he narrated:

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The pilgrim in the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in compensation for a Muhrim who intentionally versus unintentionally kills game?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi clarifies that the single compensation for intentional killing applies specifically to the initial act, while repeated unintentional kills incur separate compensations, a distinction rooted in the principle of *'amal* (action) versus *'adam al-'amal* (absence of action). This ruling is derived from the report of Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, linking the legal mechanism to divine retribution (*al-naqima*) in the Hereafter for the deliberate offender. The text serves to harmonize apparent contradictions in hadith by contextualizing them within the pilgrim's state of mind and the nature of the game killed.
